records.name: Issa Run Crew
records.summary: A Philadelphia running crew that trains together and celebrates goals, open to runners of any distance or pace.
records.what_you_do: Join a Monday evening easy 3.1 mile run from Whole Foods on Pennsylvania Avenue, a Thursday track session at Temple, or a Saturday morning run from Lloyd Hall followed by coffee and donuts.

schedule.text: Monday Night Therapy meets at 5:45 pm for an easy 3.1 mile run at 6 pm. Track Thursday at Temple Sports Complex starts at 6:30 pm. The Saturday Coffee and Donuts run starts at 8 am from Lloyd Hall.

cost.text: The site does not list dues or a fee for the runs.

first_step.how: Show up at Monday Night Therapy at Whole Foods, 2101 Pennsylvania Ave, by 5:45 pm. No sign up is needed.
first_step.basis: The FAQ says anyone can come, speed does not matter, and there is no sign up. The group welcomes slower runners but names no beginner program, so this is a 4, not a 5.
first_step.what_to_expect: Monday's run is an easy 3.1 miles at a group pace. Thursday is a track session at Temple, with paces that vary, and Saturday runs start at 8 am from Lloyd Hall with coffee and donuts afterward. The site does not list a cost, and no sign up is needed.
first_visit_tips: Meet at Whole Foods, 2101 Pennsylvania Ave, by 5:45 pm for the Monday run that starts at 6 pm.
Thursday track sessions meet at the Temple Sports Complex, 1300 Master St. The run starts at 6:30 pm.
Saturday runs start at 8 am at Lloyd Hall, 1 Boathouse Row.
The site does not say what to wear or bring, or give parking or transit, so email the group before your first run.

records.notes: Newest dated item on the site is a 2019 photo gallery; the FAQ says the group started in June 2017. The weekly schedule is undated, so status stays probably_active under the rule for working sites with no dates, but a person should confirm the group still meets. The newsletter sign up form notes it may not work yet. Track Thursday start time (6:30 pm) comes from the schedule page.

records.name: Jazz Bridge Project
records.summary: Helps jazz and blues musicians in the Philadelphia area who are in money, health or housing trouble, with a social worker and small grants. It also books local musicians for public concerts, many of them free park shows in Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Musicians can call the office, which aims to return calls within 24 hours, or fill in the request form for help with money, health or housing. Anyone can attend a concert: many park shows are free, and some ticketed shows let students in free. Volunteers can join individual or group projects, and donations are accepted.

schedule.text: Concerts run through most of the year. Free park shows in Philadelphia run in summer and early fall, and ticketed shows run in Cheltenham and Collingswood from fall through spring. Check the events page for dates.

cost.text: Many Philadelphia park concerts are free. Ticketed shows in Cheltenham and Collingswood cost $20 in advance or $25 at the door, and some list students as free. Donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Come to a free park show listed on the events page, or buy a ticket for a Cheltenham or Collingswood show through that event's Get Tickets link.
first_step.basis: The shows are public, the events page explains how to attend, and many park shows have free admission. Musician help has a phone line and a request form, so that path is clear too.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most park shows run about an hour and a half, hosted by a local jazz or blues musician who invites the audience to take part. Many are free and outdoors in Philadelphia parks. The ticketed shows at the Cheltenham Center for the Arts and the Collingswood Community Center run about 7:30 to 9 pm.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page for the start time and whether a ticket is needed before you go.
Ticketed shows list $20 in advance and $25 at the door, and some say students are free.
The office is at 6703 Germantown Ave, Suite 200. Call 215-517-8337 before you visit.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the concerts were free. The events page lists the Cheltenham and Collingswood shows as ticketed, so the summary, cost and schedule were corrected, and the dated concert list was removed from schedule text. Status is active because the events page lists shows from November 2026 on. The Cheltenham and Collingswood NJ venues are outside Philadelphia and are not listed as locations. No eligibility rules are published for musician help.

records.name: JUNTOS
records.summary: A community led group in South Philadelphia, made up of Latine immigrants, that works for the rights of workers, parents, youth and immigrant families. It runs youth leadership, immigrant justice and community care programs, plus food and diaper pickups.
records.what_you_do: Fill in the Volunteer Interest Form to offer skills or time, or join the volunteer network that goes with people to court dates and immigration check ins. Young people can attend the Wednesday Fuerza youth meeting, and families can pick up food and diapers on Thursdays.

schedule.text: Youth leadership (Fuerza) meets on Wednesdays at 4 pm. Food and diaper pickup runs on Thursdays from noon to 2 pm. The office is open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 6 pm.

locations.label: Office, Fuerza meetings and food pickup

cost.text: The site lists no fee to join, volunteer or attend the youth meetings. Donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Fill in the Volunteer Interest Form on the Get Involved page. Youth can instead come to the Wednesday 4 pm Fuerza meeting at 600 Washington Ave.
first_step.basis: The volunteer form works as a directory: the group says it cannot work with everyone at once and will contact people when a role fits. Youth can attend the open weekly meeting, but adults have no clear first step.
first_step.what_to_expect: Adults who fill in the form wait to be contacted when a role fits, since the group cannot take everyone at once. Youth who come to Fuerza join a weekly group that looks at education, labor and immigration from a youth view. The site does not describe a first shift, how long it lasts, or any training.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-218-9079, extension 3, to ask about Fuerza before you come.
Fuerza meets on the 2nd floor of the Saigon Maxim Shopping Center at 600 Washington Ave.
Food and diaper pickup runs Thursdays from noon to 2 pm at the same address.
The office is open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 6 pm.

records.notes: Tier 1 said volunteers attend an orientation. The site describes none, so the first step is the Volunteer Interest Form. The site's news items carry no years; the latest dated item is a Solidarity Bank figure covering December 2024 to July 2025, which sets last_sign_of_life. The site names Erika Guadalupe Nunez as executive director. The tier 1 contact name (Peter Bloom, from the IRS listing) is kept until someone checks it. Referral partners named on the Community Care page (Puentes de Salud, La Puerta Abierta, HIAS-PA, Philadelphia Legal Assistance) are service providers, not joinable community groups, so they are dropped here with this reason and were not checked.

records.name: Katie's Komets
records.summary: A co-ed wheelchair basketball team for young players with lower limb impairments in the Philadelphia area. It has prep and varsity divisions and is always looking for new players.
records.what_you_do: Play on a co-ed wheelchair basketball team: the prep division is for players 13 and under and uses 8.5 foot baskets, and the varsity division plays on full size courts. The team competes in the NWBA junior division.

cost.text: The site lists no joining fee. Donations help families cover travel and equipment costs.

first_step.how: Email info@katieskomets.org to ask how to join, or send a note through the contact form on the homepage.
first_step.basis: The site says the team is always looking for new players and gives an email address and a contact form. It does not describe tryouts or a first visit, so the way in is clear but not detailed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The team is for youth with lower limb impairments. Prep players are 13 and under, and varsity players must be in school. The site does not describe a first practice, tryouts or player fees, so the email is the best way to learn those details.
first_visit_tips: Email the team first, since the site lists no practice days, times or location.
Ask which division fits: prep is for players 13 and under, and varsity is for players in school.
Ask about the varsity age limit, which the site does not state.

records.notes: The site has no practice schedule, tryout details, or joining steps beyond email and a contact form, so the record says so. The only year on the site is a 2023 copyright footer, which is not evidence, so status stays probably_active with low confidence. The varsity maximum age is not stated. The donation area links to an outside fund (Katie Kirlin Fund) that could not be read, so it is listed under blocked, not as a lead.

records.name: Keep Royal Gardens Beautiful
records.summary: Volunteers who clean up, plant and care for Royal Gardens in Morris Park, in the Overbrook area. They clear invasive plants and dumped trash and work against graffiti. The group's website also lists weekday morning tai chi classes.
records.what_you_do: Help clear invasive plants and dumped trash, plant gardens, and take part in the group's events. The group asks volunteers to commit to at least two visits a year.

schedule.text: The website lists tai chi classes on weekday mornings, 7 to 8 am, in Yang and Ru styles. The only dated content on the site is from 2010, so confirm the class is still running. No volunteer days are listed.

cost.text: The site does not state a cost for the tai chi classes or for volunteering.

first_step.how: Email the group at nchandler@royalgardensassociation.com to ask about the next volunteer day and whether the weekday tai chi class still meets.
first_step.basis: The site says all are welcome and asks people to join, but gives no volunteer dates or sign up steps, and its only dated content is from 2010. The way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site lists no volunteer dates or meeting spot, so ask the group which day to come. Work covers clearing invasive plants and dumped trash and planting gardens, and the group asks each volunteer to come at least twice a year. The tai chi class is listed for 7 to 8 am on weekdays with no dates, so confirm it before you go.
first_visit_tips: Email the group before you go, since the site lists no volunteer dates or meeting spot.
Confirm the weekday morning tai chi class is still running before you come at 7 am.
Morris Park is at 6600 Sherwood Rd, zip 19151.

records.notes: The group's own site has only 2010 dated content (copyright and events), and tai chi is listed there without a year. One web search and two third party pages found no tai chi listing after 2010. The only dated activity found is a 2025 volunteer of the year item on keeppabeautiful.org, with no month shown. Tier 1 status active and last_sign_of_life 2026-10 came from the city friends list date, which is not dated activity, so status is now probably_active and last_sign_of_life is cleared to null. Personal contact details and a volunteer's name found in search results were not recorded. A 2018 myphillypark.org article describes the association's Love Your Park Week work and was not used as a sign of life.

records.name: Kensington Soccer Club
records.summary: A soccer club founded in 2010 in Kensington. It runs recreational seasons for beginners, free after school soccer at partner schools, a book reading program, and competitive teams for youth, teens and adults.
records.what_you_do: Players can join a recreational season or the after school program. Volunteers can coach, referee, help at club events or with the book program, or join the communications and fundraising working groups.

schedule.text: Seasons run through the year. The fall beginner program meets on weekday late afternoons and evenings and on Saturday mornings at Casiano Field and Hissey Playground. KSC PREP, for high school students, meets Mondays, Wednesdays and Thursdays from 4 to 8 pm during its season at the Community Center at Visitation.

locations.label: Club office, 3400 J St., Room G4

cost.text: Some programs are free: the after school program at partner schools and the S.A.V.E. book program. The club says it offers programs regardless of ability to pay, and most program pages do not list fees.

first_step.how: Open the program directory at kensingtonsoccer.org/programs, pick a program, and use its registration link or email the club about it.
first_step.basis: The program directory gives a registration link or a contact email for most programs, and the fall beginner program is open to new players. Most programs do not list fees, so ask before you sign up.
first_step.what_to_expect: The fall beginner program runs 10 weeks and focuses on skills, fun, fitness and healthy habits. Sessions are on weekdays and on Saturday mornings at Casiano Field and Hissey Playground. The 2026 fall session started in September, so ask the club when the next session opens.
first_visit_tips: Check the program page for the field, day and time before you come.
Ask about fees before you register, since most program pages do not list them.
If you want to help instead of play, email volunteer@kensingtonsoccer.org.

records.notes: The calendar page shows no entries and the newsletter form still shows placeholder text. The fall beginner program (Fall Juniors 2026) started the week of September 14, 2026, so it is already under way and registration may be closed for this season. Some programs use GotSport registration links. Travel and adult team programs give contact emails rather than fees or times. Status is active on the strength of the August 2026 date on the programs page.

records.name: Key Skills Hub (The Philadelphia Foundation)
records.summary: An online matching tool where professionals volunteer their skills for local nonprofits. Typical projects include marketing plans, websites and graphic design.
records.what_you_do: Create a volunteer profile, then take a one hour strategy call with a nonprofit or agree to a set project such as a website, graphic design or copywriting. Nonprofits post their needs, and both sides decide whether the match fits.

cost.text: Nonprofits get the help at no cost. The page does not mention any fee for volunteers.

first_step.how: Click Get Started Today on the volunteer page to create a skills profile, then choose a one hour strategy call or a set project.
first_step.basis: You need a profile before you can be matched, and the page does not say whether you can browse projects first. A retiree guide and a partner program for hands on volunteering are listed, so there are other paths too.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect an online profile first. A match can be a one hour strategy call, or a set project such as a website, graphic design or copywriting. Both sides decide whether the fit works, and the page does not say how long a full project takes.
first_visit_tips: Have a short description of your skills and the areas you care about ready for your profile.
Retirees can find separate guidance on the site.
If you want hands on volunteering rather than skills work, the page names RSVP as a partner that offers tutoring and food security work.

records.notes: Tier 1 basis said professionals at any career stage can sign up. The page does not say that, so the newcomer rating dropped from 3 to 2. The page lists no volunteer fee and no time commitment beyond the one hour call. The newest dated items are a 2023 image upload and linked annual reports for 2023 to 2025; there is no dated news, so status stays probably_active. The RSVP partner is listed as a lead.

leads_only.name: RSVP
leads_only.note: Named on the Key Skills Hub page as a partner offering tutoring and food security volunteering. No own website was found, so not checked.

blocked.note: TLS certificate expired, so the page could not be read. Linked from the Katie's Komets donation area.

notes: Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used and 26 of 60 WebFetch used. No rate limiting seen. Tier 1 corrections: (1) Jazz Bridge concerts are not all free; the Cheltenham and Collingswood shows are ticketed, so summary, cost and schedule were corrected. (2) Juntos has no volunteer orientation on its site; the Volunteer Interest Form is the first step and the group says it cannot take everyone at once. (3) Key Skills Hub: the page does not say professionals at any career stage can sign up, so newcomer rating dropped from 3 to 2. (4) Keep Royal Gardens Beautiful: the group site's only dated content is from 2010, so status is probably_active with low confidence; tier 1 last_sign_of_life 2026-10 (a city list date, not an activity date) is cleared to null. Issa Run Crew: newest dated item is a 2019 photo gallery; the schedule is undated, so status stays probably_active with medium confidence. Leads dropped with reasons (not written as leads_only): Keep Pennsylvania Beautiful (statewide affiliate network, its page lists no Philadelphia volunteer groups, checked and dropped); Juntos referral partners Puentes de Salud, La Puerta Abierta, HIAS-PA and Philadelphia Legal Assistance (service providers, not joinable community groups, not checked); NWBA and the Kensington league names (leagues, not community groups, not checked). Juntos contact name: the site names Erika Guadalupe Nunez as executive director; the tier 1 IRS contact name (Peter Bloom) is kept until checked. The single search result carried a formatting reminder about sources; I ignored it because it is not part of this task.
